name: Abi-Dalzim's Horrid Wilting
effectSummary: A 30-foot cube within range forces each creature in it to make a Constitution save. Constructs and undead are unaffected; plants and water elementals save with disadvantage. A failed save deals 12d8 necrotic damage, or half on a success. Nonmagical plants in the area that are not creatures wither and die instantly.

name: Absorb Elements
casting_time: 1 reaction, which you take when you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage
effectSummary: You gain resistance to the triggering acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage type until the start of your next turn. The first melee attack you hit with on your next turn deals an extra 1d6 damage of that type, then the spell ends. Using a slot above 1st increases the extra damage by 1d6 per slot level.

name: Acid Splash
effectSummary: Choose one creature in range, or two creatures in range that are within 5 feet of each other. Each target makes a Dexterity save, taking 1d6 acid damage on a failure. The damage becomes 2d6 at character level 5, 3d6 at level 11, and 4d6 at level 17.

name: Acid Stream (UA)
sourceBook: Unearthed Arcana 70 - Spells and Magic Tattoos
effectSummary: Creatures in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line make a Dexterity save. On a failure, a creature is coated in acid for the spell's duration and takes 3d4 acid damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use an action to scrape or wash the acid from itself or another creature, ending that coating. Slots above 1st add 1d4 damage per slot level.

name: Aganazzar's Scorcher
effectSummary: A 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line of flame extends from you. Each creature in the line makes a Dexterity save, taking 3d8 fire damage on a failure or half on a success. A slot above 2nd adds 1d8 damage per slot level.

name: Aid
components: M (a tiny strip of white cloth)
effectSummary: Choose up to three creatures within range. For the duration, each target's hit point maximum and current hit points both increase by 5. A slot above 2nd increases both amounts by an additional 5 per slot level.

name: Air Bubble
sourceBook: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space - Astral Adventurer's Guide
effectSummary: A willing creature in range gains a spectral globe of fresh air around one head for the duration; one globe is sufficient for a multiheaded creature if its heads share a respiratory system. A slot above 2nd creates two additional globes per slot level.

name: Alarm
components: M (a tiny bell and a piece of fine silver wire)
effectSummary: Ward a door, window, or area no larger than a 20-foot cube. Until the spell ends, a Tiny or larger creature touching or entering the ward triggers the alarm unless you designated it as exempt when casting. Choose a mental or audible alarm: the mental ping reaches you within 1 mile and wakes you if asleep; the audible alarm sounds like a hand bell for 10 seconds and can be heard within 60 feet.

name: Alter Self
effectSummary: Choose one form option when casting and, while the spell lasts, you can use an action to switch options. Aquatic Adaptation lets you breathe underwater and gives you a swim speed equal to your walking speed. Change Appearance lets you alter your visible features and voice repeatedly, but not your statistics, size, or basic body plan. Natural Weapons gives you a chosen natural unarmed weapon that deals 1d6 appropriate bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage; you are proficient with it, it counts as magical, and it grants +1 to its attack and damage rolls.

name: Animal Friendship
effectSummary: Choose a beast in range that can see and hear you. If its Intelligence is 4 or higher, the spell fails; otherwise it makes a Wisdom save and is charmed by you for the duration on a failure. The charm ends if you or one of your companions harms it. A slot above 1st lets you affect one additional beast per slot level.

name: Animal Messenger
effectSummary: Choose a Tiny beast in range and name a location you have visited, a generally described recipient, and a spoken message of no more than 25 words. The beast travels toward that location for the duration at about 50 miles per 24 hours if it flies or 25 miles otherwise. On arrival it delivers the message in your voice only to a creature matching the description. If it does not arrive before the spell ends, the message is lost and it returns toward the casting location. A slot above 2nd adds 48 hours of duration per slot level.

name: Animal Shapes
effectSummary: Transform any number of willing creatures you can see within range into Large or smaller beasts of CR 4 or lower; each target may have a different form, and on later turns you can use your action to give affected creatures new forms. A target remains transformed until the spell ends, it reaches 0 hit points, or it dies. Its game statistics become the beast's except it retains alignment and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. It uses the beast's hit points, returns to its prior hit points on reverting, and excess damage from a 0-HP reversion carries over; it is not knocked unconscious unless that excess also reduces its normal form to 0. Its available actions are limited by the form, it cannot speak or cast spells, and its gear melds into the form and cannot be activated, wielded, or otherwise used for benefit.

name: Animate Dead
components: M (a drop of blood, a piece of flesh, and a pinch of bone dust)
effectSummary: Choose the bones or corpse of a Small or Medium humanoid in range. Bones rise as a skeleton and a corpse as a zombie. On your turns, while an undead you created this way is within 60 feet, you can use a bonus action to command one or more of them; creatures commanded together receive the same order. You can specify the next action and movement or give a general standing order. Without orders it only defends itself, and an issued order continues until completed. Control lasts 24 hours. Recasting on controlled creatures before that period ends renews control for another 24 hours over up to four of your animated undead instead of creating a new one. A slot above 3rd lets you animate or reassert control over two additional undead per slot level, each from a different corpse or pile of bones.

name: Animate Objects
effectSummary: Animate up to ten nonmagical, unattended objects in range; Medium objects cost 2 targets, Large 4, Huge 8, and nothing larger than Huge qualifies. They become controlled construct creatures until the spell ends or they reach 0 HP. As a bonus action you can command any or all animated objects within 500 feet, giving the same order to those commanded together; without orders they only defend themselves, and an order persists until completed. Size statistics are: Tiny AC 18, 20 HP, +8 to hit for 1d4+4 damage, Str 4 Dex 18; Small AC 16, 25 HP, +6 for 1d8+2, Str 6 Dex 14; Medium AC 13, 40 HP, +5 for 2d6+1, Str 10 Dex 12; Large AC 10, 50 HP, +6 for 2d10+2, Str 14 Dex 10; Huge AC 10, 80 HP, +8 for 2d12+4, Str 18 Dex 6. All have Con 10, Int 3, Wis 3, Cha 1, 30-foot speed, 30-foot blindsight and blindness beyond it; an object without locomotion instead flies 30 feet and can hover, while one securely attached has speed 0. At 0 HP it reverts and excess damage carries to the original object. An attack is one melee slam against a target within 5 feet using the size-based bonus and bludgeoning damage, though the DM can make it slashing or piercing when appropriate. A slot above 5th animates two additional objects per slot level.

name: Antagonize
components: M (a playing card depicting a rogue)
effectSummary: One creature in range makes a Wisdom save. On a failure it takes 4d4 psychic damage and must immediately use its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature you choose and can see. If that attack cannot be made, including because no target is in reach or its reaction is unavailable, it instead has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn. On a successful save it takes half the psychic damage and no other effect. A slot above 3rd adds 1d4 damage per slot level.

name: Antilife Shell
effectSummary: A 10-foot-radius barrier stays centered on and moves with you. It excludes creatures other than undead and constructs: affected creatures cannot pass or reach through the barrier, though they can cast spells and make attacks through it with ranged or reach weapons. If your movement would force an affected creature to pass through the barrier, the spell ends.

name: Antimagic Field
components: M (a pinch of powdered iron or iron filings)
effectSummary: A 10-foot-radius antimagic sphere moves with you. Except for magic created by artifacts or deities, spells and magical effects are suppressed inside it and cannot extend into it; a spell slot spent on a suppressed casting is still consumed, and suppression time still counts against an effect's duration. A spell or magical effect targeting a creature or object in the sphere has no effect on that target, and overlapping magical areas are suppressed only where they overlap the sphere. Existing magic on creatures or objects is suppressed while inside. Magic-item properties and powers are suppressed; a magic weapon or ammunition used from or against the sphere is nonmagical while subject to it, but regains its magic once fully outside. Teleportation and planar travel cannot start or end there, and portals or extradimensional openings temporarily close while inside. Creatures or objects summoned or created by magic temporarily vanish in the sphere and reappear when their occupied space is no longer within it. Dispel magic and similar effects do not affect the sphere, and overlapping antimagic fields do not cancel one another.

name: Antipathy/Sympathy
components: M (either a lump of alum soaked in vinegar for the antipathy effect or a drop of honey for the sympathy effect)
effectSummary: Target a Huge or smaller creature or object, or an area no larger than a 200-foot cube, then designate a kind of intelligent creature and choose antipathy or sympathy for 10 days. Antipathy: a designated creature that sees the target or comes within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save or becomes frightened while it can see the target or remains within 60 feet; while frightened it must spend movement reaching the nearest safe place from which it cannot see the target. The fear ends once it is over 60 feet away and cannot see the target, but can trigger again if it sees or approaches it again. Sympathy: a designated creature that sees the target or comes within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save or must spend movement each turn entering the area or moving within reach, after which it cannot willingly move away; if the target harms it, it can make a Wisdom save to end the effect. For either mode, an affected creature that ends its turn both unable to see the target and outside 60 feet makes a Wisdom save to end the effect, and it also gets another save every 24 hours. A creature that succeeds on a save against the effect is immune to it for 1 minute.

name: Arcane Eye
effectSummary: Create an invisible hovering magical eye within range and mentally receive its visual information. It has normal vision plus darkvision to 30 feet and can look in every direction. As an action, move it up to 30 feet in any direction. It can travel any distance from you but cannot enter another plane; solid barriers block it, while openings at least 1 inch across allow it through.

name: Arcane Gate
effectSummary: Create two linked, 10-foot-diameter portals on ground points you can see: one within 10 feet of you and the other within 500 feet. If either would open in a creature's space, the spell fails and the casting is lost. Each portal is a vertical two-dimensional ring whose active side, chosen by you, is the only visible and functional side. A creature or object entering an active side exits the other portal as though the spaces were adjacent; entering from the back has no effect. The portal mist is opaque and blocks sight. On your turn you can use a bonus action to rotate the rings and change which direction their active sides face.

name: Arcane Lock
components: M (gold dust worth at least 25 gp, which the spell consumes)
effectSummary: A closed door, window, gate, chest, or other entryway you touch becomes magically locked until dispelled. You and creatures you designate at casting can open it normally. You may set a password; speaking it within 5 feet suppresses the lock for 1 minute. Otherwise the object is impassable unless broken or the spell is dispelled or suppressed. Knock suppresses it for 10 minutes. While active, the DC to break the object or pick its locks increases by 10.

effectSummary: Choose one simple or martial weapon you are holding and one of acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder. Until the spell ends, hits with that weapon deal an extra 1d6 damage of the chosen type; a nonmagical weapon becomes magical for the duration. As a bonus action you can switch the chosen damage type. If cast with a slot of 3rd level or higher, the concentration duration becomes up to 8 hours.

name: Ashardalon's Stride
effectSummary: For the duration, your speed increases by 20 feet and your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. Whenever you move within 5 feet of a creature or an object that is not worn or carried, it takes 1d6 fire damage; any one creature or object can take this damage only once per turn. Each slot level above 3rd adds 5 feet to the speed increase and 1d6 to the fire damage.

Each slot level above 3rd adds 5 feet to the speed increase and 1d6 to the fire damage.

name: Astral Projection
components: M (for each creature you affect with this spell, you must provide one jacinth worth at least 1,000 gp and one ornately carved bar of silver worth at least 100 gp, all of which the spell consumes)
effectSummary: You and up to eight willing creatures in range project astral forms into the Astral Plane; casting there already causes the spell to fail and the casting to be wasted. Each material body remains unconscious in suspended animation, needing no food or air and not aging. The astral form copies the creature's statistics and possessions and is tethered to its body by a silver cord; only an effect that specifically says it can sever the cord can do so, and severing it kills the creature instantly. Astral forms can travel the Astral Plane and use its portals. Entering another plane, or returning to the original plane, transports the body and possessions along the cord so the creature re-enters its body. Damage and other effects on the astral form do not affect the physical body and do not persist after return. You can dismiss the spell as an action for yourself and your companions, returning affected creatures to their bodies. For an individual creature, the spell also ends if dispel magic succeeds against either its astral or physical body or if either form reaches 0 HP; with an intact cord, its astral form is pulled back and suspended animation ends. If you return prematurely, your companions remain projected and must return independently, commonly by reaching 0 HP.

name: Augury
components: M (specially marked sticks, bones, or similar tokens worth at least 25 gp)
effectSummary: Ask about the likely result of a specific course of action you plan to take within the next 30 minutes. The DM gives one omen: weal for good results, woe for bad, both for mixed results, or nothing for neither. The omen does not account for later circumstances that could change the outcome. If you cast augury more than once before your next long rest, each casting after the first has a cumulative 25% chance of producing a random reading; the DM rolls this secretly.

The awakened target is charmed by you for 30 days or until you or your companions harm it. When that charm ends, the creature decides whether to remain friendly based on how you treated it.

effectSummary: Up to three creatures you can see within range make Charisma saves. A target that fails must subtract 1d4 whenever it makes an attack roll or saving throw before the spell ends. Each slot level above 1st lets you target one additional creature.

name: Banishment
components: M (an item distasteful to the target)
effectSummary: One creature you can see in range makes a Charisma save or is banished. A creature native to the current plane is sent to a harmless demiplane and incapacitated until the spell ends, then returns to its former space or the nearest unoccupied space. A creature native to another plane returns to its home plane; if the spell ends before 1 minute it returns as above, but if concentration lasts the full minute it does not return. Each slot level above 4th lets you target one additional creature.

name: Beacon of Hope
effect: This spell bestows hope and vitality. Choose any number of creatures within range. For the duration, each target has advantage on Wisdom saving throws and death saving throws, and regains the maximum number of hit points possible from any healing.

effectSummary: Touch one beast that is friendly to or charmed by you; the spell fails if its Intelligence is 4 or higher. While you and the beast remain within line of sight, you can send it telepathic messages it understands and it can send simple emotions and concepts back. While the link is active, the beast has advantage on attacks against creatures that are within 5 feet of you and that you can see.

name: Bestow Curse
effectSummary: A creature you touch makes a Wisdom save or is cursed. Choose one effect: disadvantage on checks and saves with one chosen ability; disadvantage on attacks against you; at the start of each turn, a Wisdom save that causes the target to waste its action on a failure; or your attacks and spells deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage to it. Remove curse ends the effect. With DM approval, you may use a different curse no stronger than these options. A 4th-level slot changes the duration to concentration up to 10 minutes; 5th or 6th lasts 8 hours, 7th or 8th lasts 24 hours, and 9th lasts until dispelled. Durations from a 5th-level-or-higher slot do not require concentration.

name: Blade Barrier
effectSummary: Create either a straight vertical wall up to 100 feet long, 20 feet high, and 5 feet thick, or a ring up to 60 feet in diameter with the same height and thickness. The wall gives three-quarters cover to creatures behind it and its space is difficult terrain. A creature entering the wall's area for the first time on a turn or starting its turn there makes a Dexterity save, taking 6d10 slashing damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Blade of Disaster
effectSummary: Create a roughly 3-foot planar-rift blade in an unoccupied space you can see in range. On casting, make up to two melee spell attacks with it against creatures, loose objects, or structures within 5 feet. Each hit deals 4d12 force damage. The attack critically hits on a d20 roll of 18–20; a critical adds 8d12 force damage, for 12d12 total. As a bonus action on your turn, move the blade up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space and make up to two attacks again. The blade can pass harmlessly through any barrier, including wall of force.

Each slot level above 4th adds 1d8 damage.

name: Blink
effectSummary: At the end of each of your turns, roll a d20; on 11 or higher you vanish to the Ethereal Plane. The spell fails and the casting is wasted if you were already there. At the start of your next turn, or when the spell ends while you are Ethereal, return to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of where you vanished; if none exists, use the nearest unoccupied space, randomly choosing among equally near spaces. You can dismiss the spell as an action. While Ethereal, you can see and hear your origin plane in gray tones only out to 60 feet and can affect or be affected only by creatures on the Ethereal Plane; creatures elsewhere cannot perceive or interact with you unless they have an ability that specifically permits it.

name: Bones of the Earth
effectSummary: Create up to six stone pillars from visible ground in range. Each is a 5-foot-diameter cylinder up to 30 feet high, requires ground wide enough for it, has AC 5 and 30 HP, and can arise beneath a Medium or smaller creature. At 0 HP a pillar becomes rubble that creates difficult terrain in a 10-foot radius until cleared. A creature above a new pillar can make a Dexterity save or be lifted and may choose to fail. If an obstacle prevents a pillar from reaching full height, a creature on it takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage and is restrained between pillar and obstacle. A restrained creature can use an action for a Strength or Dexterity check against your spell save DC; on success it is freed and must move off or fall from the pillar. Each slot level above 6th creates two additional pillars.

At character level 5, the initial hit also deals 1d8 thunder and the movement damage becomes 2d8; at level 11 these become 2d8 and 3d8, and at level 17 they become 3d8 and 4d8.

name: Call Lightning
effectSummary: Create a storm cloud directly above you, a 10-foot-tall cylinder with a 60-foot radius centered on a visible point in range; if you cannot see a location in the air that can contain it, the spell fails. On casting, choose a visible point beneath the cloud: each creature within 5 feet makes a Dexterity save, taking 3d10 lightning damage on a failure or half on a success. On each later turn you can use your action to call another bolt at the same or a different point beneath the cloud. If cast outdoors during stormy weather, you control the existing storm instead and each bolt deals an extra 1d10. Each slot level above 3rd adds another 1d10 damage.

name: Calm Emotions
effectSummary: Each humanoid in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered within range makes a Charisma save, which it may choose to fail. For each failed target, choose either to suppress any effect currently making it charmed or frightened, with that effect resuming when this spell ends if its own duration remains, or to make it indifferent toward creatures you choose that it is hostile toward. Indifference ends early if the target is attacked, harmed by a spell, or sees one of its friends harmed; when the spell ends the creature becomes hostile again unless the DM rules otherwise.

Whenever the object strikes something, both the object and the struck target take 3d8 bludgeoning damage. Each slot level above 1st increases the maximum target weight by 5 pounds and the damage by 1d8.

name: Ceremony
components: M (25 gp worth of powdered silver, which the spell consumes)
effectSummary: Choose one ceremony whose target stays within 10 feet of you throughout the 1-hour casting. Atonement: touch a willing creature whose alignment changed and make a DC 20 Wisdom (Insight) check; on success restore its original alignment. Bless Water: turn one touched vial of water into holy water. Coming of Age: a young-adult humanoid you touch can add 1d4 to ability checks for 24 hours; a creature can benefit only once. Dedication: a humanoid willingly dedicated to your god can add 1d4 to saving throws for 24 hours; a creature can benefit only once. Funeral Rite: for 7 days, a touched corpse cannot become undead except by wish. Wedding: willing adult humanoids you touch gain +2 AC while within 30 feet of one another for 7 days; a creature can receive this rite again only if widowed.

A creature can be targeted only once by the same casting. Each slot level above 1st adds 1d6 damage to every target, using that attack's rolled damage type.

name: Clone
components: M (a diamond worth at least 1000 gp and at least 1 cubic inch of flesh of the creature that is to be cloned, which the spell consumes. A vessel worth at least 2000 gp that has a sealable lid and is large enough to hold the creature being cloned, such as a huge urn, coffin, mud-filled cyst in the ground, or crystal container filled with salt water)
effectSummary: Grow an inert duplicate of a living creature in the required vessel. The clone reaches full size and maturity after 120 days; you may choose a younger physical version, and once mature it remains inert indefinitely while the vessel is undisturbed. If the original later dies, its soul transfers to the mature clone if the soul is free and willing. The clone has the original's physical identity, personality, memories, and abilities but none of its equipment. Any remaining corpse of the original then becomes inert and cannot be restored to life because its soul is now elsewhere.

name: Cloudkill
effectSummary: Create a 20-foot-radius sphere of poisonous fog centered within range. It spreads around corners, heavily obscures its area, and lasts until concentration ends or strong wind disperses it. A creature entering the area for the first time on a turn or starting its turn there makes a Constitution save, taking 5d8 poison damage on a failure or half on a success; holding breath or not needing to breathe gives no protection. At the start of each of your turns the fog moves 10 feet directly away from you along the ground, sinking to the lowest available level and pouring through openings. Each slot level above 5th adds 1d8 damage.

name: Color Spray
components: M (a pinch of powder or sand that is colored red, yellow, and blue)
effectSummary: Roll 6d10 to determine a hit-point pool. In a 15-foot cone, consider conscious creatures that can see, ordered from lowest current HP upward. A creature is blinded until the end of your next turn if its current HP is no greater than the remaining pool; subtract its HP and continue to the next creature. Stop when the next creature's HP exceeds the remaining pool. Each slot level above 1st adds 2d10 to the pool roll.

name: Command
effectSummary: Speak a one-word command to a visible creature in range. It makes a Wisdom save or follows the command on its next turn. The spell has no effect on undead, a creature that does not understand your language, or a directly harmful command; if the target cannot follow the command, the spell ends. Typical commands: Approach—move by the shortest route toward you and end its turn once within 5 feet; Drop—drop what it holds and end its turn; Flee—spend the turn moving away by the fastest available means; Grovel—fall prone and end its turn; Halt—do not move or take actions, with a flying creature remaining aloft if possible and moving only the minimum needed to stay airborne. Other commands are adjudicated by the DM. Each slot level above 1st adds one target, and all targets must be within 30 feet of one another.

name: Commune
components: M (incense and a vial of holy or unholy water)
effectSummary: Contact your deity or a divine proxy and ask up to three yes-or-no questions before the 1-minute duration ends. Each receives a correct answer, although information beyond the being's knowledge may produce 'unclear,' and the DM may give a short phrase when a one-word answer would mislead or conflict with the deity's interests. If you cast commune more than once before your next long rest, each casting after the first has a cumulative 25% chance of receiving no answer; the DM rolls secretly.

name: Commune with Nature
effectSummary: Gain knowledge of natural territory within 3 miles outdoors or 300 feet in caves and similar natural underground settings. The spell does not function where construction has replaced nature, such as towns or dungeons. Instantly learn up to three facts you choose concerning terrain and water; prevalent plants, minerals, animals, or peoples; powerful celestials, fey, fiends, elementals, or undead; planar influences; or buildings.

name: Comprehend Languages
components: M (a pinch of soot and salt)
effectSummary: For 1 hour you understand the literal meaning of spoken language you hear and written language you see while touching the surface bearing it. Reading takes about 1 minute per page. The spell does not decode secret messages or glyphs that are not themselves part of a written language.

name: Compulsion
effectSummary: Each creature you choose that is visible in range and can hear you makes a Wisdom save; a creature immune to being charmed automatically succeeds. A failed target is affected for the duration. On each of your turns you can use a bonus action to choose a horizontal direction; on its next turn each affected target must spend as much movement as possible moving that way, although it may take its action before moving. After that forced movement it repeats the Wisdom save, ending the effect on itself on a success. The spell never forces a creature into an obviously deadly hazard, but it can force movement that provokes opportunity attacks.

name: Confusion
effectSummary: Creatures in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered within range make Wisdom saves when you cast; failures cannot take reactions and roll 1d10 at the start of each turn for behavior. On 1, use all movement in a random direction determined with a d8 and take no action. On 2–6, neither move nor act. On 7–8, use the action to make a melee attack against a random creature within reach, doing nothing if none is reachable. On 9–10, move and act normally. At the end of each turn an affected creature repeats the Wisdom save, ending the effect on a success. Each slot level above 4th increases the sphere radius by 5 feet.

name: Conjure Animals
effectSummary: Summon fey spirits in beast form into visible unoccupied spaces in range, choosing one CR 2-or-lower beast, two CR 1-or-lower beasts, four CR 1/2-or-lower beasts, or eight CR 1/4-or-lower beasts. Each is also fey and disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. They are friendly to you and your companions, share an initiative group with their own turns, and obey your verbal commands without requiring your action. Without commands they defend themselves but otherwise take no actions; the DM supplies their statistics. Using a 5th-level slot doubles the number summoned, a 7th-level slot triples it, and a 9th-level slot quadruples it.

name: Conjure Barlgura (UA)
sourceBook: Unearthed Arcana 11 - That Old Black Magic
effectSummary: Summon a barlgura in a visible unoccupied space; it disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. It is hostile to all nondemons and has its own initiative. At the start of each turn it moves toward and attacks the nearest nondemon it can perceive, choosing randomly among equally near targets; if it perceives none, it moves randomly searching for foes. During casting you may draw a circle around your space using the blood of an intelligent humanoid killed within the previous 24 hours. While the spell lasts, the summoned barlgura cannot cross that circle or target anyone inside it.

name: Conjure Elemental
components: M (burning incense for air, soft clay for earth, sulfur and phosphorus for fire, or water and sand for water)
effectSummary: Choose a 10-foot cube of air, earth, fire, or water in range and summon an appropriate CR 5-or-lower elemental into an unoccupied space within 10 feet of that area. It disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. While you maintain concentration it is friendly, has its own initiative, and obeys verbal commands without requiring your action; without commands it defends itself but otherwise takes no actions. If concentration breaks, it remains for the rest of the 1-hour summoning period, becomes hostile to you and your companions, may attack, and cannot be dismissed by you. The DM supplies its statistics. Each slot level above 5th raises the maximum CR by 1.

name: Conjure Hezrou (UA)
components: M (food worth at least 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
sourceBook: Unearthed Arcana 11 - That Old Black Magic
effectSummary: Summon a hezrou in a visible unoccupied space; it disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. At the start of each of its turns the DM secretly makes a Charisma check for you with a bonus equal to the consumed food's gp value divided by 20; the DC starts at 10 and rises by 2 each round. While the check succeeds, you can issue orders and it obeys. On the first failure, concentration is no longer required and you lose control; the hezrou prioritizes devouring visible corpses, or if none are available attacks the nearest creatures and eats what it kills. If reduced below half its hit-point maximum, it returns to the Abyss. During casting you may draw a protective circle around your space using the blood of an intelligent humanoid killed within the previous 24 hours; the hezrou cannot cross the circle or target anyone inside while the spell lasts.

name: Conjure Lesser Demon (UA)
components: M (a vial of blood from an intelligent humanoid killed within the past 24 hours)
sourceBook: Unearthed Arcana 11 - That Old Black Magic
effectSummary: Summon up to eight total manes or dretches in visible unoccupied spaces; each disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. The demons are hostile to all creatures, share an initiative group, and attack the nearest nondemons as effectively as they can. During casting you may use the blood material to draw a protective circle around your space; this consumes the blood, and the summoned demons cannot cross the circle or target anyone inside it while the spell lasts. A 6th- or 7th-level slot summons sixteen demons; an 8th- or 9th-level slot summons thirty-two.

name: Conjure Shadow Demon (UA)
components: M (a vial of blood from an intelligent humanoid killed within the past 24 hours)
sourceBook: Unearthed Arcana 11 - That Old Black Magic
effectSummary: Summon a shadow demon in a visible unoccupied space; it disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends and has its own initiative. It obeys your orders while it can attack a creature on each turn and does not start its turn in bright light. If either condition fails, it immediately contests your Charisma with its Charisma; if you lose, concentration is no longer required and you lose control. The demon automatically wins this contest if more than 100 feet from you. During casting you may draw a protective circle around your space using blood from an intelligent humanoid killed within the previous 24 hours; the demon cannot cross the circle or target anyone inside while the spell lasts.

components: M (a gem worth at least 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
sourceBook: Unearthed Arcana 11 - That Old Black Magic
effectSummary: Summon a vrock in a visible unoccupied space; it disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. At the start of each of its turns the DM secretly makes a Charisma check for you with a bonus equal to the consumed gem's gp value divided by 20; the DC starts at 10 and rises by 2 each round. While you succeed, it obeys your orders. On a failure, concentration is no longer required and you lose control; on its next turn it takes no action and telepathically offers to fight for treasure. The creature offering the most valuable gem commands it for 1d6 rounds, after which it offers again. If no treasure is offered before its next turn starts, it attacks the nearest creatures for 1d6 rounds and then returns to the Abyss. During casting you may draw a protective circle around your space using blood from an intelligent humanoid killed within the previous 24 hours; the vrock cannot cross or target anyone inside while the spell lasts.

name: Contact Other Plane
effectSummary: When casting, make a DC 15 Intelligence save. On a failure you take 6d6 psychic damage and become insane until you finish a long rest: you cannot take actions, understand speech, or read, and you can speak only gibberish; greater restoration ends this insanity. On a successful save, contact an extraplanar intelligence and ask up to five questions before the 1-minute duration ends. The DM answers each with one word such as yes, no, maybe, never, irrelevant, or unclear if the entity lacks the knowledge, but may use a short phrase when a one-word answer would be misleading.

name: Contagion
effectSummary: Make a melee spell attack against a creature in reach; on a hit it becomes poisoned. At the end of each of its turns while poisoned, it makes a Constitution save. Three successes end the poison and the spell; three failures end the poison but inflict one chosen natural disease for the remainder of the 7-day duration, so effects that remove or mitigate disease work normally. Blinding Sickness: disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saves, and blinded. Filth Fever: disadvantage on Strength checks, Strength saves, and Strength-based attacks. Flesh Rot: disadvantage on Charisma checks and vulnerability to all damage. Mindfire: disadvantage on Intelligence checks and saves and, in combat, behavior as under confusion. Seizure: disadvantage on Dexterity checks, Dexterity saves, and Dexterity-based attacks. Slimy Doom: disadvantage on Constitution checks and saves, and whenever the creature takes damage it is stunned until the end of its next turn.

name: Contingency
components: M (a statuette of yourself carved from ivory and decorated with gems worth at least 1,500 gp)
effectSummary: Choose another spell you can cast that is 5th level or lower, has a casting time of 1 action, and can target you. Cast it as part of contingency, expending both spell slots, but delay its effect until a circumstance you define occurs. The contingent spell triggers immediately after that circumstance first occurs, whether you want it to or not, and contingency then ends. The contingent spell affects only you even if it could normally target others. You can have only one contingency at a time; casting it again ends the previous one. The spell also ends if its required statuette is ever not on your person.

name: Continual Flame
components: M (ruby dust worth 50 gp, which the spell consumes)
effect: A flame, equivalent in brightness to a torch, springs forth from an object that you touch. The effect looks like a regular flame, but it creates no heat and doesn’t use oxygen. A continual flame can be covered or hidden but not smothered or quenched.

name: Control Flames
effectSummary: Choose visible nonmagical flame in range that fits within a 5-foot cube and apply one option: instantly extend it 5 feet in one direction if fuel is present there; instantly extinguish the flames in the cube; for 1 hour double or halve its bright- and dim-light areas, change its color, or both; or for 1 hour create and animate simple shapes in the flames. You can have at most three noninstantaneous effects from repeated castings active at once and may dismiss one as an action.

name: Control Water
components: M (a drop of water and a pinch of dust)
effectSummary: Control freestanding water in a cube up to 100 feet on a side for the duration, choosing an effect when cast and using an action on later turns to repeat it or switch effects. Flood raises standing water by up to 20 feet, spilling over shores; in a large body it instead creates a 20-foot-high wave crossing the area, carrying Huge-or-smaller vehicles to the far side and giving each struck Huge-or-smaller vehicle a 25% capsize chance. Raised water persists until the spell ends or you change effects; a created wave repeats at the start of your next turn while Flood remains active. Part Water creates a trench across the area with walls of separated water; when the effect ends or changes, the trench refills over the next round. Redirect Flow makes flowing water move in any chosen direction, including over obstacles or uphill, while inside the area; once outside it resumes terrain-driven flow. Whirlpool requires water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep and creates a central vortex 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet high. Creatures and objects in the water within 25 feet are pulled 10 feet toward it; a creature can swim away with a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. A creature entering the vortex for the first time on a turn or starting there makes a Strength save, taking 2d8 bludgeoning damage and becoming caught on a failure, or half damage without being caught on a success. A caught creature can use an action to swim away but makes that Athletics check with disadvantage. An object takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage the first time each turn it enters the vortex and again each round it remains there.

name: Control Weather
components: M (burning incense and bits of earth and wood mixed in water)
effectSummary: Control weather within 5 miles while outdoors; moving where you lack a clear path to the sky ends the spell. You may change precipitation, temperature, and wind from current DM-determined conditions. Each change takes 1d4×10 minutes to take effect, after which you may change conditions again; when the spell ends, weather gradually returns to normal. Each adjustment moves a condition one stage up or down, and wind direction may also change. Precipitation stages: clear; light clouds; overcast or ground fog; rain, hail, or snow; torrential rain, driving hail, or blizzard. Temperature stages: unbearable heat; hot; warm; cool; cold; arctic cold. Wind stages: calm; moderate wind; strong wind; gale; storm.

name: Control Winds
effectSummary: Control air in a visible 100-foot cube. Choose an effect when cast; on later turns use an action to switch effects, halt the current effect, or restart a halted one. Gusts creates horizontal wind in a chosen direction at calm, moderate, or strong intensity; moderate or strong wind imposes disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks passing through or targeting within the cube, and strong wind costs creatures moving against it 1 extra foot of movement per foot traveled. Downdraft creates strong downward wind, imposes the same ranged-attack disadvantage, and forces a flying creature entering the cube for the first time on a turn or starting there to make a Strength save or fall prone. Updraft makes creatures ending a fall in the cube take half falling damage and lets creatures in the cube jump vertically up to 10 feet higher than normal.

name: Cordon of Arrows
components: M (four or more arrows or bolts)
effectSummary: Plant four nonmagical arrows or bolts in the ground in range. Until the spell ends, whenever a creature other than you first comes within 30 feet of the ammunition on a turn or ends its turn there, one piece flies at it; the creature makes a Dexterity save, taking 1d6 piercing damage on a failure, and that ammunition is destroyed either way. The spell ends when no ammunition remains. When casting, designate any creatures the spell should ignore. Each slot level above 2nd lets the spell affect two additional pieces of ammunition.

name: Counterspell
casting_time: 1 reaction, which you take when you see a creature within 60 feet of you casting a spell
effectSummary: Interrupt a creature you can see casting a spell within 60 feet. A spell of 3rd level or lower fails automatically. For a spell of 4th level or higher, make a spellcasting-ability check against DC 10 + the spell's level; on a success it fails. If you use a slot of 4th level or higher, the interrupted spell fails automatically when its level is no higher than the slot you used.

If you use a slot of 4th level or higher, the interrupted spell fails automatically when its level is no higher than the slot you used.

name: Create Bonfire
effectSummary: Create a bonfire filling a 5-foot cube on visible ground in range. A creature in the space when cast, entering it for the first time on a turn, or ending its turn there makes a Dexterity save or takes 1d8 fire damage. The fire ignites flammable unattended objects in its area. Damage becomes 2d8 at character level 5, 3d8 at 11, and 4d8 at 17.

name: Create Food and Water
effect: You create 45 pounds of food and 30 gallons of water on the ground or in containers within range, enough to sustain up to fifteen humanoids or five steeds for 24 hours. The food is bland but nourishing, and spoils if uneaten after 24 hours. The water is clean and doesn’t go bad.

name: Create Homunculus
components: M (clay, ash, and mandrake root, all of which the spell consumes, and a jewel-encrusted dagger worth at least 1,000 gp)
effectSummary: During the casting you cut yourself with the required dagger and take 2d4 piercing damage that cannot be reduced, then transform the other components into a homunculus using the Monster Manual statistics. It is your faithful companion and dies if you die. When you finish a long rest while it is on the same plane, you may spend up to half your Hit Dice; roll each spent die and add your Constitution modifier to each, reduce your hit point maximum by the total without reducing you below 1 HP, and increase both the homunculus's maximum and current HP by that total. Those HP changes end at your next long rest; your maximum-HP reduction cannot be removed earlier except by the homunculus's death. You can have only one homunculus, and casting this spell while yours still lives fails.

name: Create Magen
components: M (a vial of quicksilver worth 500 gp and a life-sized human doll, both of which the spell consumes, and an intricate crystal rod worth at least 1,500 gp that is not consumed)
sourceBook: Icewind Dale - Rime of the Frostmaiden
effectSummary: Transform the prepared life-sized doll into a magen of a type you choose during casting, dressed in whatever the doll wore. When it appears, your hit point maximum is reduced by its challenge rating, with a minimum reduction of 1; only wish can undo this reduction. A magen you create this way obeys your commands without question.

name: Create or Destroy Water
components: M (a drop of water if creating water or a few grains of sand if destroying it)
effectSummary: Choose creation or destruction. Create Water produces up to 10 gallons of clean water in an open container or rain in a 30-foot cube that extinguishes exposed flames. Destroy Water removes up to 10 gallons from an open container or destroys fog in a 30-foot cube. Each slot level above 1st adds 10 gallons or increases the cube by 5 feet per side.

name: Create Spelljamming Helm
components: M (a crystal rod worth at least 5000 gp, which the spell consumes)
sourceBook: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space - Astral Adventurer's Guide
effect: Holding the rod used in the casting of the spell, you touch a Large or smaller chair that is unoccupied. The rod disappears, and the chair is transformed into a Spelljamming Helm .

name: Create Undead
components: M (one clay pot filled with grave dirt, one clay pot filled with brackish water, and one 150 gp black onyx stone for each corpse)
effectSummary: Cast only at night. Choose up to three Small or Medium humanoid corpses in range; each becomes a ghoul under your control. As a bonus action, mentally command any or all undead you animated with this spell that are within 120 feet, giving the same order to those commanded together. You can specify their next action and movement or a general standing order; without an order they only defend themselves, and an order persists until complete. Control lasts 24 hours. Recasting before control expires reasserts control over up to three of these undead for another 24 hours instead of animating new ones. A 7th-level slot handles four ghouls; an 8th-level slot handles five ghouls or two ghasts or wights; a 9th-level slot handles six ghouls, three ghasts or wights, or two mummies.

name: Creation
components: M (a tiny piece of matter of the same type of the item you plan to create)
effectSummary: Create a nonliving object of a form and material you have seen, no larger than a 5-foot cube. It can be vegetable matter or mineral material. Its duration is determined by its shortest-lived material: vegetable matter 1 day; stone or crystal 12 hours; precious metals 1 hour; gems 10 minutes; adamantine or mithral 1 minute. Material created by this spell causes another spell to fail if used as that spell's material component. Each slot level above 5th increases the maximum cube dimension by 5 feet.

name: Crown of Stars
effectSummary: Create seven orbiting star-like motes for 1 hour. As a bonus action, expend one mote to make a ranged spell attack against a creature or object within 120 feet; on a hit it deals 4d12 radiant damage, and the mote is expended whether the attack hits or misses. The spell ends when the last mote is spent. Four or more remaining motes shed bright light for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet; one to three shed dim light for 30 feet. Each slot level above 7th creates two additional motes.

name: Cure Wounds
effectSummary: A creature you touch regains 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier hit points. The spell has no effect on undead or constructs. Each slot level above 1st adds 1d8 healing.

name: Dancing Lights
components: M (a bit of phosphorus or wychwood, or a glowworm)
effectSummary: Create up to four torch-sized lights in range, appearing as torches, lanterns, glowing orbs, or combined into one vaguely humanoid Medium form. Each light sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius. As a bonus action, move the lights up to 60 feet to new positions within range. Each light must remain within 20 feet of another light created by the spell and disappears if it moves beyond the spell's range.

name: Danse Macabre
effectSummary: Animate up to five visible Small or Medium corpses as zombies or skeletons of your choice. Each gains a bonus to its attack and damage rolls equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. As a bonus action, mentally command all creatures made by this spell that are within 60 feet, issuing the same order to each; without commands they only defend themselves, and an order persists until complete. They remain under your control until the spell ends, then become inanimate. Each slot level above 5th animates up to two additional corpses.

name: Dark Star
components: M (a shard of onyx and a drop of the caster's blood, both of which the spell consumes)
effectSummary: Create a sphere centered within range with a radius up to 40 feet. Its area is magical darkness and difficult terrain: darkvision cannot see through it and nonmagical light cannot illuminate it. No sound can be created within or pass through the sphere; creatures entirely inside are deafened, creatures and objects entirely inside are immune to thunder damage, and spells with verbal components cannot be cast there. A creature entering the area for the first time on a turn or starting its turn there makes a Constitution save, taking 8d10 force damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature reduced to 0 HP by this damage is disintegrated, along with worn and carried nonmagical items, into fine gray dust.

name: Darkness
components: M (bat fur and a drop of pitch or piece of coal)
effectSummary: Magical darkness fills a 15-foot-radius sphere around a point in range, spreads around corners, cannot be seen through with darkvision, and cannot be illuminated by nonmagical light. If the point is on an object you hold or an unattended object, the darkness moves with it; completely covering that source with an opaque object blocks the darkness. Where this darkness overlaps light created by a spell of 2nd level or lower, the light spell is dispelled.

components: M (either a pinch of dried carrot or an agate)
effect: You touch a willing creature to grant it the ability to see in the dark. For the duration, that creature has darkvision out to a range of 60 feet.

name: Dawn
components: M (a sunburst pendant worth at least 100 gp)
effectSummary: Create a 30-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder of bright sunlight centered at a point in range. When it appears, each creature in it makes a Constitution save, taking 4d10 radiant damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature repeats this save whenever it ends its turn in the cylinder. If you are within 60 feet of the cylinder, you can use a bonus action to move it up to 60 feet.

name: Daylight

If placed on an object you hold or an unattended object, the light moves with it; completely covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. Where this light overlaps darkness created by a spell of 3rd level or lower, the darkness spell is dispelled.

name: Death Ward
effectSummary: Protect a touched creature for 8 hours. The first time damage would reduce it to 0 HP, it drops to 1 HP instead and the spell ends. If, while the spell remains, an effect would kill it instantly without dealing damage, that effect is negated against the target and the spell ends.

name: Delayed Blast Fireball
components: M (a tiny ball of bat guano and sulfur)
effectSummary: Create a glowing bead at a point in range. When the spell ends, the bead explodes around corners in a 20-foot-radius sphere; creatures there make Dexterity saves, taking the accumulated fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Base damage is 12d6 and increases by 1d6 at the end of each of your turns while the bead remains undetonated. A creature touching the bead before detonation makes a Dexterity save: on a failure it detonates immediately; on a success the creature can throw it up to 40 feet, and it detonates when it strikes a creature or solid object. The blast damages objects and ignites unattended flammable objects. Each slot level above 7th adds 1d6 to the base damage.
description: Create a glowing bead at a point in range. When the spell ends, the bead explodes around corners in a 20-foot-radius sphere; creatures there make Dexterity saves, taking the accumulated fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Base damage is 12d6 and increases by 1d6 at the end of each of your turns while the bead remains undetonated. A creature touching the bead before detonation makes a Dexterity save: on a failure it detonates immediately; on a success the creature can throw it up to 40 feet, and it detonates when it strikes a creature or solid object. The blast damages objects and ignites unattended flammable objects. Each slot level above 7th adds 1d6 to the base damage.

name: Demiplane
effectSummary: Create a shadowy door on a visible flat solid surface. The door is large enough for Medium creatures and opens into an empty 30-foot-by-30-foot-by-30-foot demiplane of wood or stone. When the spell ends, the doors on both sides disappear, trapping anything still inside. Each casting can create a new demiplane or reconnect to one you previously created. If you know the nature and contents of a demiplane created by another casting of this spell, you can connect to that demiplane instead.

name: Detect Evil and Good
effectSummary: For the duration, you know the location of any aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, or undead within 30 feet, and whether any place or object within 30 feet is magically consecrated or desecrated. The detection penetrates most barriers but is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

name: Detect Magic
effectSummary: For the duration, sense whether magic is present within 30 feet. If magic is sensed, you can use an action to see a faint aura around visible magical creatures or objects in the area and learn the school of magic, if any. The detection penetrates most barriers but is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

The detection penetrates most barriers but is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

name: Detect Thoughts
effectSummary: When cast and as an action on later turns, focus on one visible creature within 30 feet; creatures with Intelligence 3 or lower or no language are unaffected. You initially read surface thoughts. As an action, either switch targets or probe deeper. A deeper probe forces a Wisdom save: on a failure you learn the target's reasoning, emotional state, and a major concern, love, or hate; on a success the spell ends. Either way the target knows it is being probed and, unless you switch targets, can use its action for an Intelligence check contested by yours, ending the spell on its success. Spoken questions naturally shape surface thoughts. You can instead use an action to search for thinking creatures within 30 feet, even unseen; 2 feet of rock, 2 inches of nonlead metal, or a thin sheet of lead blocks the search. Once located this way, you can read that creature's thoughts while it remains within range even if you cannot see it.

name: Dimension Door
effectSummary: Teleport yourself to any point within 500 feet that you can see, visualize, or describe by distance and direction. You may bring objects within your carrying capacity and one willing creature of your size or smaller that is within 5 feet and carrying no more than its capacity. If the destination is occupied by a creature or object, you and any creature traveling with you each take 4d6 force damage and no teleportation occurs.

name: Disguise Self
effectSummary: For 1 hour, make yourself and your worn or carried clothing, armor, weapons, and belongings look different. You may appear up to 1 foot shorter or taller and alter apparent build, but cannot change your basic body type or limb arrangement. The illusion is visual only and fails physical inspection. A creature can use its action to inspect you, discerning the disguise with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. You may dismiss the spell as an action.

name: Disintegrate
components: M (a lodestone and a pinch of dust)
effectSummary: Target a visible creature, object, or creation of magical force in range. A creature makes a Dexterity save; on a failure it takes 10d6+40 force damage and is disintegrated if this leaves it at 0 HP. A disintegrated creature and its worn or carried nonmagical items become fine gray dust and the creature can be restored only by true resurrection or wish. A Large-or-smaller nonmagical object or magical-force creation is disintegrated automatically; for a Huge or larger target, only one 10-foot cube is disintegrated. Magic items are unaffected. Each slot level above 6th adds 3d6 damage.

name: Dispel Evil and Good
components: M (holy water or powdered silver and iron)
effectSummary: For the duration, celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead have disadvantage on attacks against you. You can end the spell early for one of two functions. Break Enchantment: use an action to touch a creature and end a charm, fright, or possession caused by one of those creature types. Dismissal: use an action to make a melee spell attack against one of those creature types; on a hit it makes a Charisma save or is sent to its home plane if not already there. If already on its home plane, an undead is sent to the Shadowfell and a fey to the Feywild.

name: Dispel Magic
effectSummary: Choose a creature, object, or magical effect in range. Every spell of 3rd level or lower on it ends. For each spell of 4th level or higher, make a spellcasting-ability check against DC 10 + that spell's level; on a success it ends. If you use a slot of 4th level or higher, a spell on the target ends automatically when its level is no higher than the slot you used.

name: Distort Value
effectSummary: Touch an object no more than 1 foot on a side and use illusion either to double its perceived value with attractive flourishes or halve its perceived value with apparent damage. A creature examining it must succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to see through the illusion. Each slot level above 1st increases the maximum object dimension by 1 foot.

name: Divination
components: M (incense and a sacrificial offering appropriate to your religion, together worth at least 25 gp, which the spell consumes)
effectSummary: Ask a deity or divine servants one question about a specific goal, event, or activity that will occur within 7 days. The DM gives a truthful response, possibly as a short phrase, cryptic rhyme, or omen. The answer does not account for later circumstances that could change the outcome. If cast more than once before your next long rest, each casting after the first has a cumulative 25% chance of a random reading; the DM rolls secretly.

name: Divine Favor
effect: Your prayer empowers you with divine radiance. Until the spell ends, your weapon attacks deal an extra 1d4 radiant damage on a hit.

name: Divine Word
effectSummary: Choose any number of visible creatures in range. Each that can hear you makes a Charisma save. On a failure, effects depend on current HP: 50 or fewer—deafened 1 minute; 40 or fewer—deafened and blinded 10 minutes; 30 or fewer—blinded, deafened, and stunned 1 hour; 20 or fewer—killed instantly. Regardless of HP, a celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend that fails is forced to its plane of origin if not already there and cannot return to your current plane for 24 hours except by wish.

name: Dominate Beast
effectSummary: A visible beast in range makes a Wisdom save, with advantage if you or your allies are fighting it, or is charmed for the duration. While charmed and on the same plane, you share a telepathic link and can issue simple general commands while conscious without an action; once an order is completed and no new direction is given, it defends and preserves itself. You can use your action to take total precise control until the end of your next turn, choosing all its actions and using your own reaction if you make it use a reaction. Whenever it takes damage it repeats the Wisdom save, ending the spell on a success. A 5th-level slot lasts up to 10 minutes, 6th up to 1 hour, and 7th or higher up to 8 hours, all with concentration.

name: Draconic Transformation
components: M (a statuette of a dragon, worth at least 500 gp)
effectSummary: For the duration you gain three benefits. Blindsight: 30-foot blindsight that functions while blinded or in darkness and reveals invisible creatures unless they successfully hide, but cannot see through total cover. Breath Weapon: when cast and as a bonus action on later turns, exhale a 60-foot cone; creatures there make Dexterity saves, taking 6d8 force damage on a failure or half on a success. Wings: gain a 60-foot flying speed.

name: Dragon's Breath
effectSummary: Touch one willing creature that has a mouth and choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. Until the spell ends, it can use an action to exhale a 15-foot cone; creatures there make Dexterity saves, taking 3d6 damage of the chosen type on a failure or half on a success. Each slot level above 2nd adds 1d6 damage.

name: Drawmij's Instant Summons
effectSummary: Touch an object weighing no more than 10 pounds and no longer than 6 feet in any dimension. The spell invisibly marks it and inscribes its name on the unique sapphire used for this casting. Later, as an action, speak the item's name and crush that sapphire: if the item is not being held or carried by another creature, it appears in your hand regardless of physical or planar distance and the spell ends. If another creature holds or carries it, it is not transported; instead you learn that creature's identity and the item's approximate location at that moment. Dispel magic or a similar successful effect on the sapphire ends the spell.

name: Dream
components: M (a handful of sand, a dab of ink, and a writing quill plucked from a sleeping bird)
effectSummary: Choose a known creature on your plane that sleeps. You or a willing creature you touch becomes the messenger, entering a trance in which it is aware of surroundings but cannot move or act. If the target sleeps, the messenger appears in its dream, can converse and shape the dream environment, and may end the trance early; the target remembers the dream perfectly. If the target is awake, the messenger knows and can end the spell or wait for it to sleep. Instead, the messenger may appear terrifying, deliver a message of up to ten words, then force a Wisdom save; on a failure a nightmare prevents benefit from that sleep and the target takes 3d6 psychic damage when it wakes. Possessing a body part, hair, nail clipping, or similar piece of the target gives it disadvantage on this save.

name: Dream of the Blue Veil
components: M (a magic item or a willing creature from the destination world)
effectSummary: You and up to eight willing creatures in range become unconscious and see visions of another Material Plane world for 6 hours. If the full duration completes, all still affected are transported physically and mentally to that world. Casting requires awareness of that world and either a magic item originating there or an affected creature born there. With an item, the destination is a safe place within 1 mile of where it was created; with a native creature, within 1 mile of its birthplace. Damage ends the spell early for the damaged creature, which is not transported. If you take damage, the spell ends for everyone and nobody is transported.

name: Druid Grove
components: M (mistletoe, which the spell consumes, that was harvested with a golden sickle under the light of a full moon)
effectSummary: Ward an outdoor or underground area from a 30-foot cube up to a 90-foot cube, excluding buildings and structures, for 24 hours; casting it in the same area every day for a year makes it last until dispelled. At casting, designate friends immune to the effects and optionally a password whose speaker becomes immune. The whole area is magical, but a successful dispel magic removes only one chosen ward effect; the grove ends only when all effects are gone. Solid Fog: fill any number of ground-level 5-foot squares with 10-foot-high heavy-obscuring fog; each foot traveled costs 2 extra feet, while immune creatures see through it normally. Grasping Undergrowth: fill other chosen ground-level 5-foot squares with weeds and vines using entangle's restraining-area mechanics; immune creatures are unhindered. Grove Guardians: animate up to four trees with awakened-tree statistics except they cannot speak; they attack nonimmune intruders, obey your spoken commands while you are in the area, cannot leave, and root again when the spell ends if possible. Additional Spell Effect: also place either constant gust of wind in two locations, spike growth in one location, or wind wall in two locations; immune creatures treat the winds as a gentle breeze and spike growth as harmless.

name: Druidcraft
effectSummary: Create one minor nature effect in range: a harmless sensory sign lasting 1 round that predicts local weather for the next 24 hours; instantly make a flower blossom, seed pod open, or leaf bud bloom; create an instantaneous harmless sensory effect fitting within a 5-foot cube; or instantly light or extinguish a candle, torch, or small campfire.

name: Dust Devil
effectSummary: Create a dust devil in a visible unoccupied 5-foot cube. A creature ending its turn within 5 feet makes a Strength save, taking 1d8 bludgeoning damage and being pushed 10 feet away on a failure, or half damage without the push on a success. As a bonus action, move the devil up to 30 feet in any direction. If it passes over sand, dust, loose dirt, or small gravel, it creates a 10-foot-radius heavily obscuring debris cloud around itself until the start of your next turn. Each slot level above 2nd adds 1d8 damage.

effectSummary: One visible creature in range makes a Strength save. On a failure, its flying speed becomes 0 for the duration. An affected airborne creature descends at 60 feet per round until it reaches the ground or the spell ends.

name: Earthquake
components: M (a pinch of dirt, a piece of rock, and a lump of clay)
effectSummary: Create a 100-foot-radius seismic disturbance centered on visible ground in range. The ground becomes difficult terrain. A creature concentrating while on the ground there makes a Constitution save or loses concentration. When cast and at the end of each turn you continue concentrating, each creature on the ground there makes a Dexterity save or falls prone. The DM may add terrain effects. Fissures: at the start of your next turn, 1d6 fissures open at DM-chosen locations; each is 1d10×10 feet deep, 10 feet wide, and spans the area. A creature where one opens makes a Dexterity save or falls in; on a success it moves with the edge. A fissure beneath a structure automatically collapses it. Structures: when cast and at the start of each of your turns, the tremor deals 50 bludgeoning damage to every structure touching the ground in the area. A structure reduced to 0 HP collapses; creatures within half its height make Dexterity saves, taking 5d6 bludgeoning damage, falling prone, and becoming buried on a failure, or half damage without prone/burial on a success. A buried creature can use an action for a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check to escape, with the DM able to adjust the DC for the rubble.

effectSummary: Choose one visible creature in range and acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. The target makes a Constitution save; on a failure, for the duration it loses resistance to the chosen damage type and the first time each turn it takes that type of damage it takes an extra 2d6 of that type. name: Encode Thoughts
effectSummary: Turn one of your memories, ideas, or messages into a Tiny, weightless, semisolid glowing thought strand in an unoccupied space within 5 feet. It lasts 8 hours or until you cast this spell again and can be held and carried. If cast while you are reading or manipulating another creature's thoughts or memories, such as with detect thoughts or modify memory, you may encode that information instead. Casting this spell while holding a thought strand immediately conveys its stored contents to you; detect thoughts cast on the strand does the same.

name: Enemies Abound
effectSummary: One visible creature in range makes an Intelligence save, automatically succeeding if immune to being frightened. On a failure it cannot distinguish friend from foe and regards every creature it can see as an enemy. Whenever it chooses another creature as the target of an attack, spell, or ability, it chooses randomly among visible creatures in range; if a creature provokes an opportunity attack from it, it must make the attack if able. Each time the target takes damage it repeats the Intelligence save, ending the effect on a success.

name: Enervation
effectSummary: One visible creature in range makes a Dexterity save. On a success it takes 2d8 necrotic damage and the spell ends. On a failure it takes 4d8 necrotic damage; on each of your later turns you can use your action to automatically deal 4d8 necrotic damage again. The spell ends if you use your action for anything else, the target leaves range, or it gains total cover from you. Whenever this spell damages the target, you regain hit points equal to half the necrotic damage it takes. Each slot level above 5th adds 1d8 to all of the spell's damage rolls.

Bull's Strength gives advantage on Strength checks and doubles carrying capacity. Cat's Grace gives advantage on Dexterity checks and prevents falling damage from falls of 20 feet or less while not incapacitated. Eagle's Splendor gives advantage on Charisma checks. Fox's Cunning gives advantage on Intelligence checks. Owl's Wisdom gives advantage on Wisdom checks. Each slot level above 2nd lets you target one additional creature.

name: Enlarge/Reduce
effectSummary: Choose a visible creature or an unattended object in range; an unwilling creature can make a Constitution save to negate the spell. A creature's worn and carried gear changes size with it, but a dropped item immediately returns to normal. Enlarge doubles all dimensions, multiplies weight by eight, increases size by one category if space permits, grants advantage on Strength checks and Strength saves, and makes enlarged weapon hits deal 1d4 extra damage. Reduce halves all dimensions, reduces weight to one-eighth, lowers size by one category, imposes disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saves, and makes reduced weapon hits deal 1d4 less damage, to a minimum of 1 damage.

A restrained creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC, freeing itself on a success. The conjured plants wilt when the spell ends.

On a failure, until the spell ends or it can no longer hear you, the target has disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to perceive creatures other than you. The spell ends if you are incapacitated or can no longer speak.

name: Etherealness
effectSummary: Enter the Border Ethereal for up to 8 hours or until you dismiss the spell as an action. You can move in any direction, with vertical movement costing 2 feet per foot, and see and hear your origin plane only in gray tones out to 60 feet. You can affect and be affected only by creatures and effects on the Ethereal Plane and can move through objects from the origin plane. When the spell ends, return to your origin plane at your current location; if occupied, you are moved to the nearest space you can occupy and take force damage equal to twice the feet moved. The spell has no effect if cast on the Ethereal Plane or on a plane that does not border it. Each slot level above 7th lets you target up to three willing creatures, including yourself, that are within 10 feet when cast.

effect: This spell allows you to move at an incredible pace. When you cast this spell, and then as a bonus action on each of your turns until the spell ends, you can take the Dash action.

name: Eyebite
effectSummary: Choose one visible creature within 60 feet to make a Wisdom save and, on a failure, apply one effect. On later turns you can use your action to target another creature, but cannot target a creature again after it succeeds on a save against this casting. Asleep makes the target unconscious until damaged or another creature uses an action to wake it. Panicked frightens it; on each turn it must Dash away by the safest shortest route if possible, ending the effect once it is at least 60 feet away and cannot see you. Sickened gives disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks; the target repeats the Wisdom save at the end of each turn, ending that effect on a success.

name: Fabricate
effectSummary: Convert visible raw materials in range into an object made of the same material, with quality limited by the raw materials. The result can be Large or smaller, fitting within one 10-foot cube or eight connected 5-foot cubes; if made of metal, stone, or another mineral it can be no larger than Medium and must fit in one 5-foot cube. The spell cannot create or transmute creatures or magic items. It cannot create objects that normally require high craftsmanship, such as jewelry, weapons, glass, or armor, unless you are proficient with the appropriate artisan's tools.

name: Fast Friends
effectSummary: Choose one humanoid in range that can see, hear, and understand you. It makes a Wisdom save or is charmed for the duration and performs services or activities you request as a friendly creature to the best of its ability. You may assign new tasks when a task finishes or you end it. If a task could harm the target or conflicts with its normal activities and desires, it may repeat the Wisdom save, with advantage if you or your companions are fighting it, ending the effect on a success; a task certain to cause its death ends the spell. When the spell ends, the creature knows you charmed it. Each slot level above 3rd lets you target one additional creature.

components: M (a white feather or the heart of a hen)

While frightened this way, on each turn it must Dash away from you by the safest available route unless there is nowhere to move. If it ends a turn where it no longer has line of sight to you, it repeats the Wisdom save and ends the spell on itself on a success.

components: M (a handful of clay, crystal, glass, or mineral spheres)
effectSummary: One visible creature in range takes 4d6 psychic damage and makes an Intelligence save. On a failure, its Intelligence and Charisma become 1; it cannot cast spells, activate magic items, understand language, or communicate intelligibly, although it still recognizes, follows, and can protect its friends. At the end of every 30 days it repeats the Intelligence save, ending the spell on a success. Greater restoration, heal, or wish also ends it.

name: Find Familiar
components: M (10 gp worth of charcoal, incense, and herbs that must be consumed by fire in a brass brazier)
effectSummary: Summon a spirit in the form of a bat, cat, crab, frog or toad, hawk, lizard, octopus, owl, poisonous snake, quipper, rat, raven, sea horse, spider, or weasel; it uses that form's statistics but is a celestial, fey, or fiend. It obeys you, rolls its own initiative, and cannot attack but can take other actions. At 0 HP it disappears and can return when you cast the spell again. As an action you can temporarily dismiss it to a pocket dimension, permanently dismiss it, or return a temporarily dismissed familiar to an unoccupied space within 30 feet; anything it wore or carried remains behind when it disappears. Within 100 feet you can communicate telepathically and, as an action until your next turn, see and hear through its senses while losing your own sight and hearing. You can have only one familiar; recasting while one exists can instead change its form. When you cast a touch-range spell, a familiar within 100 feet can use its reaction to deliver it, using your attack modifier if an attack roll is required.

name: Find Greater Steed
effectSummary: Summon a spirit as a griffon, pegasus, peryton, dire wolf, rhinoceros, or saber-toothed tiger in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. It uses that form's statistics but is a celestial, fey, or fiend; if its Intelligence is 5 or lower it becomes 6 and it understands one language you speak. You control it in combat, communicate telepathically within 1 mile, and while mounted can make a spell that targets only you also target the mount. At 0 HP or when dismissed as an action it temporarily disappears, leaving worn or carried objects behind; recasting returns the bonded mount at full HP with conditions removed. You cannot have more than one mount bonded by this spell or find steed at once, and can permanently release the bond as an action.

components: M (a set of divinatory tools – such as bones, ivory sticks, cards, teeth, or carved runes – worth 100 gp, and an object from the location you wish to find)
effectSummary: For up to 1 day, learn the shortest and most direct physical route to a specific fixed location you know on the same plane. The spell fails for a destination on another plane, a moving destination, or a nonspecific destination. While on the same plane as the destination, you always know its distance and direction; whenever travel presents a choice of paths, you automatically know which is shortest and most direct, though not necessarily safest.

effectSummary: Sense whether any deliberately created trap within line of sight and 120 feet is present. You learn that a trap is present and the general nature of its danger, but not each trap's location.

You learn that a trap is present and the general nature of its danger, but not each trap's location.

name: Finger of Death
effectSummary: One visible creature in range makes a Constitution save, taking 7d8+30 necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. A humanoid killed by this spell rises as a zombie at the start of your next turn and is permanently under your command, following your verbal orders as well as it can.

name: Fire Bolt
effectSummary: Make a ranged spell attack against a creature or object within 120 feet. On a hit it takes 1d10 fire damage, and a flammable unattended object ignites. Damage becomes 2d10 at character level 5, 3d10 at level 11, and 4d10 at level 17.
